tasks.readingPassage:
Confirmation Bias

Confirmation bias is a cognitive tendency in which people favor information that confirms their existing beliefs while disregarding or undervaluing evidence that contradicts those beliefs. This bias can affect decision-making in areas ranging from personal relationships to scientific research, often leading individuals to form and maintain inaccurate conclusions despite available contrary evidence.
tasks.listeningTranscript: Professor: Let me give you an example of confirmation bias in action. Imagine a manager who believes that employees who arrive early are more productive. Every time she notices an early employee doing good work, she mentally notes it as proof she's right. But when an early employee makes a mistake, she tends to overlook it or explain it away as an unusual exception. Meanwhile, if a late-arriving employee does excellent work, she might dismiss it as luck rather than updating her belief. Over time, this selective attention reinforces her original assumption, even though she's not actually looking at the full picture of everyone's performance.
tasks.prompt: Explain confirmation bias using the example of the manager given by the professor.

tasks.listeningTranscript: Professor: Today let's discuss the concept of a keystone species in ecology. A keystone species is one that has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its population size. A well-studied example is the sea otter in kelp forest ecosystems along the Pacific coast. Sea otters prey on sea urchins, which in turn feed on kelp. When sea otter populations declined sharply in the 20th century due to hunting, sea urchin populations exploded unchecked, and they consumed vast amounts of kelp, leading to what scientists call 'urchin barrens'—areas where kelp forests had once thrived but were reduced to bare rock. When otter populations later recovered in certain areas due to conservation efforts, urchin populations were brought back under control, and the kelp forests were able to regenerate, along with the many other species that depend on kelp for habitat.
tasks.prompt: Using the example of the sea otter, explain what a keystone species is and why it matters to an ecosystem.
